title: Deep learning measures the thoracic aorta in cardiac MRI to enable genetic analysis
summary: A deep-learning model measured ascending and descending thoracic aortic dimensions in 4.6 million UK Biobank cardiac magnetic resonance images. Genome-wide association studies in 39,688 individuals identified 82 loci for ascending and 47 for descending aortic diameter (14 overlapping), and further analyses prioritized genes including SVIL. A polygenic score for ascending aortic diameter was associated with thoracic aortic aneurysm in 385,621 UK Biobank participants (hazard ratio 1.43 per s.d., 95% CI 1.32-1.54). Deep learning is the phenotyping step, and the findings are genetic associations in one biobank.
ai_technology: Deep-learning model measuring aortic dimensions in cardiac magnetic resonance images
organization: Broad Institute; Harvard University; Massachusetts General Hospital

evidence.tested: Genome-wide association, rare-variant and polygenic score analyses using deep-learning-derived aortic measurements in the UK Biobank.
evidence.unknown: Replication outside the UK Biobank and functional confirmation of prioritized genes; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Deep learning produced the quantitative aortic diameter phenotypes.
